canvasSizing: The phone never sizes the store to the screen. initFilmDecoder line 1023 sets heroFilm to the encode's 720x900 and the phone branch of sizeFilmCanvas keeps it there (viewport 720x900, ts = 1/720,1/900, bc = 0 so the Catmull-Rom path is off), which makes each paint one texture upload plus one quad at 0.65 Mpx and leaves scaling to the compositor. The dpr cap at line 887 (2) and the 3840 cap (891) are therefore not exercised on the phone; on a 3x iPhone the 720 store is shown at up to 1.9x while the text is over it (blurred still on top anyway) and at ~1.24x at the hold once --hz has pulled the frame to .66, which is where crispness matters. The CSS box does the portrait crop: `.hero__frame` is `position:sticky; top:0; height:100svh` inside the 240svh absolute `#hero`, and the canvas (and the fallback <video>) is an object-fit:cover box of the encode's 4:5 aspect: `left:50%;top:50%;width:max(100%,calc(100svh*.8));height:max(100svh,calc(100vw/.8));transform:translate(-50%,-50%);object-fit:cover;object-position:50% 53%` (on 390x844 that is 675x844, showing the middle 58% of the crop while the text is in front, then the whole crop as the frame scales to .66; on 844x390 landscape it is 844x1055 cropped to the middle 37% of the height, which still holds the mark because the mark spans y 35-72% of the crop and object-position centres on 53%). Because the crop is already cloche-centred, object-position is 50% horizontally, so the same rules also render the desktop 16:9 asset acceptably if a rotated tablet ever hands it over before the reload. The frame's scale and the blur/scrim opacities are custom properties on #hero (--hz, --hb, --hs) written by pDraw through setVar, so they are compositor-only changes: no layout, no paint, and getBoundingClientRect is never read on the scroll path (heroTop/pinRange are cached by phoneMeasure). Orientation change: the gates keep a phone in story, resize fires after 140 ms, phoneMeasure re-reads heroTop and pinRange (100svh changes, so the pin's scroll length changes), the store is untouched, and pDraw repaints the current u. 100svh needs iOS 15.4+/Chrome 108+; declare `height:100vh` first as the fallback. Never use 100dvh here (it would resize the frame during the toolbar collapse).

risks.risk: iOS Safari 16.4-16.x: WebCodecs VideoDecoder exists but VideoFrame as a WebGL texImage2D source may throw, and today's catch at site.js 873 would abandon the decoder for the seek fallback.
risks.mitigation: Phone-gated recovery in blit(): swap in a cloned canvas with a 2D context and drawImage(VideoFrame) (supported from 16.4), only then filmFallback(). Report which path ran through __pfilm.state().twoD. iOS cannot be driven from this Windows machine, so one real-iPhone check is needed; ask Karan to open ?bare=1 on his phone and read __pfilm.state() from the Safari inspector, or add a hidden `?pfilm=dbg` readout.

risks.risk: Safari ignores hardwareAcceleration:'prefer-software' and decodes through VideoToolbox, so each 8-frame GOP pays a hardware flush; if the average passes 90 ms after six groups the existing check (1145-1147) hands the film to the <video> element.
risks.mitigation: That fallback is acceptable behaviour (scrub by currentTime, 60-150 ms per seek, never blocks scrolling); keep the threshold, log FD.slowMs, and only revisit it with numbers from a real device.

risks.risk: iOS <video> with preload="none" (template line 187) stops at HAVE_METADATA and never fires loadeddata, so the fallback would stay at opacity 0 behind the still.
risks.mitigation: Phone-gated preload='auto' before load(), seek from loadedmetadata, mark ready on the first seeked. The still remains as the placeholder so a failure is invisible rather than black.

risks.risk: A tablet rotating across the film/story boundary: the phone asset is loaded, then enableFilm() runs on the desktop stage. With today's heroInit guard the desktop would scrub the cropped 4:5 phone film.
risks.mitigation: initHero(url) keyed on heroSrc plus dropHero(); disablePhoneFilm() drops the phone asset so enableFilm loads the desktop one. Test in cdp.js by emulating 768x1024 touch, then 1024x768 with touch off (c.size), asserting heroSrc flips and the store returns to 1920x1080.

risks.risk: Memory: the decoder keeps 32 frames (keepGops 4 x 8); at 1080p that is ~100 MB plus a 3.9 MB byte array and a Blob copy on fallback, which older iPhones and 3 GB Androids will evict.
risks.mitigation: The 720x900 encode makes it ~31 MB; dropFrames() on visibilitychange frees it in the background; dropHero() closes the decoder when the phone film stops.

risks.risk: Desktop pixel parity (constraint 1): the changes touch shared functions (sizeFilmCanvas, blit, useVideoElement, initHero, applyMode, the resize/visibility handlers).
risks.mitigation: Every new branch is behind phoneOn or html.story.pfilm; on desktop phoneOn is always false, so each shared function follows its old lines. Prove it: pixel-diff desktop stills at three __feel.at() moments before and after, run friction-check.js and verify-live.js, and diff the rendered index.html against the previous build (expect only the new <picture> inside .hero__frame, the __PHONE head lines and the two tokens).

risks.risk: position:sticky inside the absolute #hero: html,body carry overflow-x:hidden/clip (site.css 70). On the root that propagates to the viewport and sticky still works in current browsers, but no other story element uses sticky today.
risks.mitigation: Verify on the first headless run at 390x844 (the frame's rect.top must read 0 through the pin) and on the iPhone check. Fallback if a browser misbehaves: the driver already knows u, so it can switch .hero__frame to position:fixed while 0<u<1 and back to absolute at the ends.

risks.risk: Runtime blur alternative (filter: blur() on the frame fading with scroll) is the direct reading of 'the background is a bit blurred out'; the plan uses a blurred still cross-fade instead because a per-frame GPU blur of a 1.3 Mpx layer (780x1688 at dpr 2) is 2-6 ms on mid phones and risks the scroll frame rate.
risks.mitigation: Build it as a local toggle (?pfilm=cssblur) so Karan can compare on his own phone; if he prefers it, cap the blur at 10 px and drop --hb to 0 by u=.3 so the cost vanishes early. The film stays sharp in the file either way.

risks.risk: The phone film's first screen overlaps the hero text; the cloche's bright rim and the top-of-frame bar lights can fight the 'fully visible' text if the scrim is too light.
risks.mitigation: The scrim is a custom property (--hs) with its gradient in one CSS rule, so it is tuned by eye on the 390x844 stills; run the copy/contrast probe on pf-0.png (headline, sub, buttons over the darkest and brightest hero frames) and keep the top 40% at >= .55 darkening while u < .1.

risks.risk: Hostinger's CDN re-encodes JPEGs (noted in RESUME.md), so hero-still-m.jpg will not hash-match live; the mp4 should.
risks.mitigation: verify-live.js already treats JPEGs as visual-compare; add hero-scrub-m.mp4 to its hash list and hero-still-m.jpg to the JPEG list.

risks.risk: Landscape phones (story via gate 4, 100svh ~390 px): the 4:5 cover box is 844x1055 and the mark is ~180 px tall, small but complete; portrait tablets get a 768x960 box where the 720 store is upscaled ~2.1x at dpr 2.
